title: Randomized comparison of inpatient pain management in single-stage KTEP replacement surgery.
summary:
Local infiltration anesthesia (LIA), continuous postoperative regional anesthesia with nerve-femoralis catheter (NFK) and a combination of both methods are available for pain therapy in single-stage knee joint replacement operations. Both LIA and NFK are regularly performed in our clinic for knee joint replacement operations. In LIA, the surgeon injects (infiltrates) a mixture of a local anesthetic and magnesium to prolong the effect, as well as two drugs to reduce bleeding into the surgical site at the end of the operation. The NFK is placed directly before the operation and remains in place until the 4th/5th day after the operation. In this study, the two methods will be compared with regard to the mobilization of the new joint replacement. Further aims are to record the pain relief, to document the frequency of complications and to evaluate the necessity of the administration of oral painkillers and their side effects. In order not to falsify the results by pre-selection, patients will be randomly assigned to one of the pain therapies (randomized). The day after surgery, they are given a pedometer to record the number of steps. In addition, two days after the operation, a force meter is used to measure the strength of the quadriceps femoris muscle on both sides. To do this, the patient must sit on the bed and stretch the respective leg upwards. 
This is to record the functionality, i.e. the mobility of the (new) joint, in order to enable a comparison between the two methods. The data on pain, consumption of analgesics, etc. are collected in the clinical routine for the study project. In addition, patients are asked to fill out a questionnaire to their satisfaction.
conditions: Mechanical complication due to a joint endoprosthesis: knee joint
Revision of an endoprosthesis at the knee joint

interventions.name: 1. LIA group: patients are injected with LIA (local infiltration analgesia)
2. NFK group: Patients receive a NFK catheter (N. femoralis catheter).
3. LIA+NFK group: Patients receive both analgesia procedures in combination.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Single stage KTEP change operation
- Age: 18 - 85 years
Exclusion criteria:
- Known mental illness 
- Known diseases of the cardiovascular system that lead to limitations in the ability to work under stress
- Known dementia
- Known drug abuse
- Intraoperative or postoperative complications that limit function or exercise capacity (e.g. hemodynamically relevant bleeding, circulatory or respiratory complications)
